interpretation: Every workflow hazard is represented. 7 hazards have at least one trained model card, 4 have a usable hazard-specific research model, 7 have usable component research evidence, 7 have at least one usable research model, and 3 have no trained model evidence. Zero models are independently validated for operational use. Coverage is not predictive validity.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML contributes next-day rainfall screening and a continuous precipitation estimate as forcing evidence only. Neither is a flood-occurrence, inundation, depth, or impact prediction.
limitations: Rainfall is not a flood observation; drainage, river level, and inundation outcomes are absent.
The weather model is trained at one reanalysis grid point and does not transfer automatically.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML screens 24-hour rapid intensification and estimates continuous wind change from storm-grouped best-track research. It does not predict track, landfall, surge, or local wind at a specific place.
limitations: IBTrACS is a post-event best-track reanalysis, not an operational forecast.
Rapid intensification is rare; held-out event counts are small.

entries.interpretation: The aftershock model uses a seven-day future-label-window embargo at temporal split boundaries. Any reported score is research-only on a single temporal holdout, not independent validation. It screens aftershock occurrence only after an observed mainshock; it does not predict mainshocks or ground shaking.
limitations: The corrected split purges labels whose seven-day outcome windows cross train/validation/test boundaries; results still have only one temporal holdout.
The USGS catalogue is regionally clipped and capped at 20,000 events.
Aftershock screening applies only after an observed mainshock and does not predict mainshock occurrence or ground shaking.

entries.interpretation: No defensible supervised landslide model is released: the inventory is a reported-event catalogue without a representative non-event sample.
limitations: Reported-event catalogues are biased toward populated areas and accessible roads.
No background/non-event sample exists in the repository.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML screens high-temperature events and estimates next-day maximum temperature at the Kochi reanalysis grid point. Neither is an official heatwave declaration, health-impact estimate, or warning.
limitations: Reanalysis grid-point temperature is not a station observation or an official heatwave index.
Humidity, night-time temperature, and local exposure are not modelled.

entries.interpretation: The retrained model uses a future-only 30-observation rainfall-deficit target. Its single temporal holdout is research evidence only, not independent validation or a drought declaration. It represents meteorological rainfall deficit, not agricultural or hydrological drought.
limitations: The corrected target sums the next 30 observations only; it is a meteorological rainfall-deficit proxy, not a validated drought-impact target.
A 30-day rainfall deficit is not agricultural or hydrological drought.
Soil moisture, evaporative demand, storage, and water demand are absent.

entries.interpretation: No defensible supervised model is released: facility-level release labels, controls, and representative non-events are unavailable.
limitations: No quality-controlled release inventory or facility control data are available.
Permits do not establish current emissions or causal source contribution.

entries.interpretation: No defensible supervised model is released: asset condition, network state, and outage/recovery labels are unavailable.
limitations: No verified asset condition, dependency, outage, or restoration dataset is joined.
Mapped roads and facility directories are not an exposure or vulnerability model.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML provides an exploratory concurrent cyclone-proximity/rainfall association. It is not a joint probability, lead-time forecast, or compound impact estimate.
limitations: Cyclone proximity and rainfall are concurrent; the association model has no lead time.
Only 128 cyclone-near days and about 20 compound extreme-rain days are available.
Separate component indicators are not added into a joint probability.

entries.interpretation: Shared ML contributes rainfall screening as forcing evidence only. The deterministic Rational Method flow/capacity comparison remains the decision calculation.
limitations: Drainage capacity and failure state are user-supplied assumptions, not observed.
The Rational Method comparison is a scenario calculation, not a validated flood forecast.
